localChanges: Computer players take their turns about a quarter quicker late in the game: they no longer list a square's surroundings, flood a continent, size up their units or work out a city's output more than once a turn (closes #316, closes #317, closes #408). Sending a unit somewhere with GoTo starts sooner, because the route is planned once rather than twice (closes #307), and working out what a city can build checks far fewer rules (closes #185).

log: Moved out of simple-ai-client (civ-clone/web-renderer#198, #200) unchanged apart from imports: Dependencies (with dependenciesFor), Knowledge (with MartialLawPolicy), Memory (with UncalmedReason), MemoryRegistry, actionLookup, the survey (its StrategyNote key stays 'simple-ai-client:survey' so saved games resume), the unit turn context, orders, reachable, AIStrategy, isUnitAction, unitTurnContextFor, and the Mission type with nearest and pursue. The library-unit imports are now the base-unit-type-* / base-unit-action-* classes they re-export.

New: UnitOrder (a PlayerAction<Unit> for a standing order, never a mandatory action), OrderStrategy with findStrategy and isOrderStrategy, followPath (a synchronous mover that only moves, honours canReturnAfter, and reports arrived / blocked / threatened / out-of-moves) and enemyAdjacent (the test that wakes a sleeping unit).

`pursue` flooded the unit's whole continent or sea (`reachableTiles`) for every unit given a mission, for each mission it was offered: about 90 floods a computer turn on web-renderer's turn-287 save, 6% of the turn (civ-clone/web-renderer#316). `reachableTiles` takes the turn now: given it, what it finds from a tile the unit could move on to is kept for the turn and shared by every tile of that continent or sea, by kind (land or sea), so callers must only ask it `has`. From anywhere else, such as a land unit aboard a ship, it's found afresh, as it isn't one continent. Without the turn, nothing changes. `pursue` passes the turn.

No rule turns land into sea or sea into land, so the sets are the ones a fresh flood finds; they're dropped each turn all the same. web-renderer's conformance run is unchanged, checksums and ids alike.

New rules on core-city's `TileWorked` and `TileReleased`, which `WorkedTileRegistry` processes for every tile a city starts or stops working, emit `city:tile-worked` and `city:tile-released` with the city and the tile, as `city:created` and the rest are emitted. A client sends the tile, whose `workedBy` changed, from them (civ-clone/web-renderer#138). Needs core-city 0.1.22.

Each rule names its improvement, and the one that stops a city building a second of the same names CityImprovement, so units, wonders and spaceship parts no longer check it. The criteria are unchanged and still decide.
Needs the core-city-build release that lets Build take items.
civ-clone/web-renderer#185
Each rule names its part (or Part, for the two that apply to every part), so CityBuild checks a part against its own rules rather than all ~100. The criteria are unchanged and still decide.
Needs the core-city-build release that lets Build take items.
civ-clone/web-renderer#185
Each rule names its unit (or Naval, for the coastal one), so CityBuild checks a unit against its own two or three rules rather than all ~100. The criteria are unchanged and still decide.
Needs the core-city-build release that lets Build take items.
civ-clone/web-renderer#185

The goto criterion searches for a route to decide whether GoTo is on offer, and GoTo#perform then searched for the same route again. The criterion now keeps the route it found, and the effect hands it to the GoTo through a PlannedPathFinderRegistry (lib/): its path finder returns that route for the first search for the same unit, start and end, and searches as before for anything else. base-unit-action-goto is unchanged.

Every action's criteria are validated before any effect runs, so the route is kept with the unit, from and to it was found for, and the effect only uses one that matches. Performed from anywhere other than where it was offered, the GoTo searches again, as before.

On the turn-287 save, 157 GoTos by the human player's land units to their furthest city on the same land mass take 157 searches instead of 314, and every unit ends on the same tile (civ-clone/web-renderer#307).

The route a GoTo was offered with is dropped as soon as a unit moves, is created, destroyed or changes hands, or a city is created, destroyed or captured, anywhere. A GoTo performed after that searches again, so it never follows a route through a tile that has since been occupied. A GoTo performed straight after it was offered still costs one search (civ-clone/web-renderer#307).

Each rule names its wonder (or Wonder, for the one-per-game rule, and Nuclear for the Manhattan Project one), so CityBuild checks a wonder against its own rules rather than all ~100. The criteria are unchanged and still decide.
Needs the core-city-build release that lets Build take items.
civ-clone/web-renderer#185

`WorkedTileRegistry` processes `TileWorked` (`[City, Tile]`) after each tile it registers, and `TileReleased` after each one it unregisters. `unregister` is overridden, so `unregisterByTile` is covered, and a worked tile that isn't registered releases nothing. Every way a tile comes to be worked or released goes through the registry (founding, growth, shrinking, `changeWorkedTile`, `reassignWorkers`, an enemy unit in the way, a city destroyed), so a client can follow `workedBy` from these without the callers changing (civ-clone/web-renderer#138).
Both are notifications. Unlike `TileReassigned`, nothing processing them should change which tiles are worked.

Loading a save processes nothing. `hydrate` restores membership through `register`, but makes each `WorkedTile` with `Object.create`, which never calls the constructor. `WorkedTile` keeps a `WeakSet` of the ones it constructed, and `isRestored` answers for the rest. A restored tile still processes `TileReleased` when it's later unregistered.
Once per tile, not once per call: `assignWorkers` registers one tile per call anyway, and the only many-tile `register` is the load.

`WorkedTileRegistry` skipped `TileWorked` for a tile restored from a save for the object's whole lifetime, so registering it, unregistering it and registering it again processed only `TileReleased`. The restoration mark is now consumed by the first registration, which is the one loading a game performs. Registering the same object again later is an ordinary change and processes `TileWorked`.

CityBuild#available() checked every available item against every Build rule (~100 rules x ~76 items = ~7,750 validate calls per city, nearly all of them for a different item). A criterion is an opaque function, so the only way to skip them is for the rule to say what it is about.

Build now takes items (the classes themselves, so Warrior or Wonder) among its constructor values. A rule that declares some is only checked for those items and anything extending them (Build#mayApplyTo); a rule that declares none is checked for every item, as before. The criterion still runs and still decides for the items the rule is checked for, so a declaration only narrows it and an undeclared ruleset behaves exactly as it did.

buildRulesFor() keeps the rules for each item against the array RuleRegistry#get hands back, which is a new array whenever a rule is registered, unregistered, enabled or disabled, so nothing needs invalidating.
civ-clone/web-renderer#185

The survey asks `shouldBuildCity` about every tile the player knows, every turn (23k calls on the turn-287 save), and each call built a radius-2 `Tileset` to score and, for a site that scored well enough, a radius-4 one to look for cities in. Building them was over half of the survey (civ-clone/web-renderer#317). `surroundingArea` lists a tile's surroundings once, as `Tile#getSurroundingArea` does (same tiles, same order, each once on a map small enough to wrap), since the map's shape doesn't change. Each tile's score as part of a site's surroundings is kept with the yields list it was worked out from, and worked out again once `Tile#yields` hands back a new one (after `clearYieldCache`), so every candidate site within two tiles of it reuses it.

`buildItemInCity` flooded the city's continent once or twice for every city, every decision. `continentOf` finds each continent once a turn and shares the set between its tiles (civ-clone/web-renderer#316); callers only ask it `has`. No rule turns land into sea or sea into land, but the cache is dropped each turn all the same. From a sea tile it isn't kept, as that isn't one continent.
Same decisions: web-renderer's conformance run is unchanged, checksums and ids alike.

civ1-treasury's Spend rule for units now asks the rules whether the city is in civil disorder. Registered without a registry, it asked the game-wide one, where an earlier test file's civil disorder rules, bound to that file's city growths, threw "Wrong number of CityGrowths returned" for this suite's cities: 10 tests failed in CI on master after a fresh install. The suite's own registry holds its own civil disorder rules.

The Explorer check asked for the city's continent before `reachableLandToExplore` could answer 0 for an empty list of tiles to explore, so the first city on a continent each turn flooded it for nothing when no Settler check needed it either (a size-one city, say). The list is checked first now, and the continent is only looked up with something to explore.

civ-clone/web-renderer#307 proposed caching stepCost per (from, to) for the life of a search. There is nothing for it to save: generate() costs a tile's neighbours only when it expands the tile, and the done set expands each tile once, so every step is costed exactly once per search. On the turn-287 save, the second turn after load costs 99,879 steps in 85 searches with no repeat inside any search. The test pins that, and stepCost's comment says why there is no cache.
